title: core.audio.package — the sound world index
description: The splat-foley asset-package manifest, adopted verbatim as the index of an entity's sound world (see F:/splat-foley splatfoley/package.py build_manifest, FORMAT 'splat-foley-asset' VERSION 2). It lists the described objects, the effect plan and every take with its role and score. Inside a werk package it is redundant with MANIFEST.json for file discovery and that redundancy is deliberate: this node remains an island (law 3) that a sound tool can consume with no werk knowledge at all, and the werk manifest remains the authority on which bytes exist. Where they disagree, MANIFEST.json wins and a reader MUST report the discrepancy. CAREFUL: this schema and core.audio.effect.schema.json use DIFFERENT NAMES FOR THE SAME VALUE, permanently. Here the prompt is effects[].prompt; in the per-effect sidecar it is prompt_used. The full mapping table is in spec/SPEC.md section 3.9. This index is the authority on the SET of effects; the sidecar named by effects[].meta is the authority on any ONE of them.

version.description: splat-foley package format version. 2 is what werk profile 1 was written against.

asset.description: Source asset slug. Advisory; the werk entity's identity is manifest.entity.uuid.

source.description: Original source file name the sound world was derived from.

model.description: Path of the source 3D file inside the original splat-foley package. Inside a werk package the geometry is a core.geom.* node and this field is historical record.

views.description: Rendered orbit views the description and effect plan were derived from. These are the inputs whose hashes feed the node's input_hash (law 5).

objects.description: The described objects and their materials — the vision model's reading of the asset. INFERRED, always.

provenance.description: 'segment' when the object came from a SAM segment rather than the whole-asset description.

part_of.description: Name of the parent object, for sub-objects.

bbox.description: [x, y, width, height] in PIXELS of the named view, origin at the top-left. The order is x,y,w,h and NOT x0,y0,x1,y1; stating it is the whole point of this schema existing.

part_id.description: werk addition (optional): resolves this described object to a manifest part.

object_dir.description: Slugified object name used as the audio subdirectory.

refined.description: Mirror of the per-effect sidecar's 'refined' block; see core.audio.effect.schema.json for its fields.

meta.description: Path of the per-effect sidecar validated by core.audio.effect.schema.json.

role.description: 'best' is the take a player uses. 'raw' is the pre-refinement original, kept for A/B. 'variation' is an alternative generation.

node_id.description: werk addition (optional): the core.audio.effect node that owns this effect's bytes.

counts.description: Declared totals. A reader MUST compare them against the arrays and report a mismatch — a cheap truncation detector, in the spirit of law 8's corollary.

preview_effect.description: werk addition (optional): slug of the one-shot chosen as the package's hover preview, written early in the container per the preview-first byte layout (law 9).
